label: prf:feynman-categorical-trace
title: Proof of Feynman transition amplitude as categorical trace
html:
By (Markov identification), the Markov-weighted sum of seminormal block traces equals \mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(\rho(\beta)\bigr). Only partitions with at most two rows carry nonzero weight, and on those w_\lambda = \dim_q(V_\lambda)/\dim_q(V^{\otimes n}). The partitions of n with at most two rows are (n - k, k) for 0 \leq k \leq \lfloor n/2 \rfloor, so there are \lfloor n/2 \rfloor + 1 terms.

The rule for \sigma_n^{-1} follows from the quadratic relation \sigma_n^{-1} = \sigma_n - h: \mathrm{tr}_M(x\sigma_n^{-1}) = \mathrm{tr}_M(x\sigma_n) - h\,\mathrm{tr}_M(x) = (z - h)\,\mathrm{tr}_M(x).

By (categorical mass as Markov trace), the categorical mass at a single brane level is |\mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta))|, which by the first step is the absolute value of the eigenbasis amplitude. \square
